move: donut track draws, arc fills to 72% with counter, pulses, unwinds
how: A white card holds a 300px SVG donut (grey track circle plus a blue round-capped arc, rotated -90deg) with a big percentage in the centre and a text panel with two legend rows on the right. The card scales in from 0.92/opacity:0 (power3.out) in the first 15%; the track draws around with DrawSVG 0% to 100% (expo.out) at 2-22%; the arc fills drawSVG 0% to 72% over 9-46% with expo.inOut while a tween on a plain object drives the centre percent and the Used/Available GB numbers in lockstep. Heading, paragraph and rows slide up y:14 with stagger 0.08. At 52% the arc stroke-width pulses 26 to 30 yoyo (sine.inOut). At 78% the arc unwinds to 0% and the numbers count back down with expo.in, then the card fades out with a slight scale 0.96.
adapt: Set TARGET (percent), the centre caption, heading/paragraph and the legend labels and the 512 GB capacity math; change the arc colour in .arc and .dot; keep the 1.5s expo.inOut fill and the symmetric expo.in unwind.
port: mount(el, shot) inserts the card with the SVG circles (r=130, stroke-width 26) and the text panel; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with fill at 0.09-0.46 of D, pulse at 0.52, unwind at 0.78. Needs DrawSVGPlugin registered; the second counter tween reuses the first tween's onUpdate via tl.getTweensOf(o)[0].vars.onUpdate, which is simpler as a named function. Scope getElementById to el.
caveats: arc unwinds and card fades so the last frame differs from the first (card exits, then would pop back)
